question.problem:
Find the solution to the inequality $\frac{1-7x}{5}\ge 2.$

The solution is $x$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-7x}{5} & \ge 2 \\ 5\cdot (\frac{1-7x}{5}) & \ge 5\cdot 2 \\ \cancel{5}\cdot (\frac{1-7x}{\cancel{5}}) & \ge 10 \\ 1-7x & \ge 10\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles.

Remember, when we divide an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-7x & \ge 10 \\ 1-7x-1 & \ge 10-1 \\ -7x & \ge 9 \\ \frac{-7x}{-7} & \,\,\le \,\,\frac{9}{-7} \\ x & \le -\frac{9}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x\le -\frac{9}{7}.$
